I farm 35 mu of chrysanthemum, and this year I will keep the whole area in chrysanthemum because that is the crop I know best and it matches my irrigation conditions. I have been farming a long time, my education level is high, and my household labor is only one person, so I will keep the plan simple, standardized, and manageable. With well irrigation, I will rely on stable water supply to support establishment and flowering, and I will use improved seedling material rather than traditional stock because I want more uniform plants and a steadier flower yield. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and easier to manage alone at the start of the season. On fertilizer, I will apply a moderate but solid nutrient program with nitrogen for vegetative growth, phosphorus for rooting and early vigor, and potassium for stem strength and flower quality. I will not run an extreme input strategy; I would rather aim for stable output and controllable costs. I will also keep pest control regular because chrysanthemum quality matters, especially in the flower stage. My goal is a dependable, good-quality harvest rather than the highest possible yield.
